title: Hybrid IO floor + paused-burst crediting for hosted API pricing experiment
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: validate a hybrid per-token floor that blends ingress (input) and egress (output/streaming) rates and a short-duration 'paused-burst' crediting mechanism to reduce customer friction for spiky streaming workloads. Motivations: customers complain about unpredictable monthly bills due to asymmetric token patterns (heavy input prep + short streaming output) and enterprise contracts that want predictable floors without blocking bursty real-time features. This experiment tests whether a blended floor plus a small pool of burst credits for paused streams (streams that resume within N minutes) reduces churn and increases committed revenue without materially harming host economics.
acceptance_criteria: Primary: >=5% incremental committed MRR from pilot cohort vs. control over 6 weeks, normalized for usage growth
No statistically significant increase in support volume (>15% from baseline) related to billing confusion
Billing engine correctly calculates blended floor for 99.99% of test accounts (roll forward validation)
Implementation does not increase median token metering latency by >10ms at 95th percentile
steps: Design pricing matrix: define input rate, output rate, blended floor formula, paused-burst credit rules (credit window, credit size)
Finance to validate unit economics (model net revenue at 50/30/20 input/output mixes)
Eng ticket: implement metering flags and billing hook, feature flag gating for pilot orgs (dependency ENG-23598)
Legal: prepare enterprise contract amendment language for pilots and floor billing disclosures
Onboard 10 pilot accounts (mix of startups, mid-market, and 1 enterprise) for 6-week test
Run experiment, collect telemetry, weekly reviews with ops/finance/support
Analyze and propose next-step (scale/rollback/iterate) with recommended contract terms
metrics: Primary metric: delta committed MRR per pilot org vs control cohort
Churn propensity: 30d churn rate for pilot vs control
Billing disputes: count of billing tickets flagged as 'floor confusion'
Adoption: percentage of eligible orgs that opt into paused-burst flow during pilot
Cost sensitivity: change in average cost-per-token after credits applied
rollout_plan: Start behind a feature flag for 10 pilot orgs (2 weeks monitoring). Expand to 100 orgs if no regressions in billing logic or support volume after week 3. Safety kills: auto-revert feature flag and trigger billing backfill script if billing-logic mismatch rate >0.01% or >15% increase in billing disputes. For enterprise pilot accounts, apply contract amendment and manual reconciliation window to avoid surprise charges. Final production rollout contingent on finance/legal sign-off and an engineering postmortem on telemetry coverage.
notes: Paused-burst crediting: definition = if a streaming session pauses and resumes within 10 minutes, up to 2MB equivalent of output token credits applied once per org per day (configurable). Purpose: reduce penalty for real-time reconnections or mobile resume use-cases.

Blended floor formula proposal: floor = max(monthly_min, floor_pct * (input_tokens * input_rate + output_tokens * output_rate)). Floor_pct initially 0.75 in experiment to avoid overly aggressive upsell.
Legal asks: transparent line items on invoice showing floor contribution and credits applied; enterprise amendments must include opt-out clause for paused-burst credits
Telemetry: need new billing event 'floor_applied' and 'paused_burst_credit' with org_id, invoice_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, credit_amount, calculated_floor
